business_problem: thyssenkrupp Intellectual Property works to protect the group's IP while identifying technology gaps, supporting inventors, and analyzing extensive patent information efficiently.
solution_summary: The article reports that thyssenkrupp Intellectual Property uses AI to make its work more efficient. It describes AI processing information from patent databases, scientific publications, and other technological resources to identify patterns, trends, relationships, and potential gaps or “white spaces” in technology fields. The resulting analysis can inform research and development priorities, trend predictions, and combinations of knowledge across disciplines. The article also describes AI-assisted structured interviews with inventors and targeted questions to help complete invention disclosure forms. For patent protection, it discusses image recognition and text analysis to monitor products, services, and patents for possible infringement. No AI product, data store, deployment architecture, or named system integration is identified; storage and technical implementation details are therefore unspecified.
data_flow: Patent databases, scientific publications, and other technological resources are analyzed by AI systems to identify patterns, trends, relationships, and potential technology gaps for IP staff and R&D planning. AI is also described as supporting inventor interviews and invention disclosure forms; image recognition and text analysis can be applied to monitoring products, services, and patents for possible infringement. Storage and system interfaces are not specified.
business_outcome: AI is reported to make IP work more efficient and can help shorten the time from an idea to an invention disclosure; no measured results are provided.

source_references.title: Bringing Ideas to Market with the Help of Artificial Intelligence

evidence_quotes: The thyssenkrupp Intellectual Property team itself also utilises artificial intelligence to make its work more efficient.
AI systems can process and analyse large volumes of data from patent databases, scientific publications and other technological resources.

Once these ideas are available, artificial intelligence can be used to conduct a structured interview with the inventors and support the completion of invention disclosure forms with targeted questions.
This can significantly shorten the time from the idea to the invention disclosure
